[TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/05/20 (Sat) 13:34  
[FACT] User is currently working on a scale model of a '69 Mustang Mach 1.  
[PREFERENCE] User is looking for advice on applying custom decals received from a fellow model builder.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant provided a detailed guide on how to apply custom decals successfully, including 10 steps: prepare the surface, choose the right setting solution, cut out the decal, soak the decal, apply the decal, blot excess water, apply setting solution, smooth out air bubbles, allow to dry, and seal with a topcoat.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Additional tips provided by the assistant include handling decals by the edges, avoiding application over raised or recessed areas, and practicing to improve skills.  
[PREFERENCE] User appreciates the detailed guide provided by the assistant.  
[FACT] User received some photo-etched parts from the same fellow model builder.  
[PREFERENCE] User is excited to incorporate the photo-etched parts into their model and is seeking advice on bending and shaping them accurately.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant provided advice on handling and preparing photo-etched parts, including handling with care, cleanliness, and studying the instructions.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant provided a detailed guide on bending and shaping photo-etched parts, including using the right tools, annealing the parts (optional), bending in small increments, using a bending jig, and shaping and forming.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant provided assembly and attachment tips, including using a strong adhesive, careful positioning, and using a clamp or weight if needed.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Additional tips included bending PE parts to distribute stress evenly, avoiding sharp creases, and practicing to improve skills.  
[PREFERENCE] User is concerned about the safety aspect of annealing the PE parts and is seeking more information on how to do it safely.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant provided a detailed guide on how to anneal PE parts safely, including safety precautions, the annealing process, and post-annealing steps.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Safety precautions include protecting oneself with safety glasses, working in a well-ventilated area, using a heat-resistant surface, and avoiding overheating.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The annealing process involves holding a flame about 1-2 inches away from the PE part, heating it to a temperature between 400°F (200°C) and 500°F (260°C), holding for a few seconds, and quenching in cold water.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Important notes included that not all PE parts require annealing and that some may be too thin or delicate to anneal.
